bigPicture: Five families cover almost every function in first-year calculus: **power, polynomial, exponential, logarithmic, trigonometric**.
Polynomials: factor to find roots; quadratics via the **quadratic formula** and the **discriminant Δ**.
**Exponential and logarithm are inverses**; use their rules (not intuition) to solve equations – and check the domain.
Trig functions are **periodic**; use the **unit circle** and **reference angles**.

concepts.name: Power functions
concepts.simple: x², x³, √x, 1/x … are all ‘x to some power’. Even powers make a U, odd powers an S through the origin.
exam: **Definition:** f(x) = xᵃ, a ∈ ℝ, is a power function of degree a.
- Integer a > 0: **even** a → symmetric “U”; **odd** a → “S”-shape through the origin.
- Negative a (e.g. x⁻¹): domain excludes 0, hyperbola-like shape.
- Rational a (e.g. x^(1/2) = √x): domain restricted to x ≥ 0.

concepts.name: Polynomials and roots
concepts.simple: A polynomial is a sum of powers of x. Its roots are where the graph hits the x-axis; a degree-n polynomial has at most n of them.
exam: **Definition:** p(x) = aₙxⁿ + aₙ₋₁xⁿ⁻¹ + ⋯ + a₁x + a₀, aₙ ≠ 0, n ∈ ℕ, aᵢ ∈ ℝ; n is the **degree**. Domain always ℝ.
- A degree-n polynomial has **at most n real roots** (p(x) = 0; graph crosses or touches the x-axis).
- **Factoring:** p(x) = aₙ(x − r₁)(x − r₂)⋯(x − rₙ) if all roots rᵢ are real.

concepts.name: The quadratic formula
concepts.simple: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the discriminant b² − 4ac tells you how many solutions there are; the formula gives them.
exam: For ax² + bx + c = 0, a ≠ 0: **x₁,₂ = (−b ± √Δ)/(2a)**, **Δ = b² − 4ac** (discriminant).
- Δ > 0: two distinct real roots · Δ = 0: one repeated real root · Δ < 0: no real roots.

concepts.name: Exponential functions
concepts.simple: aˣ grows fast if a > 1 and shrinks towards 0 if 0 < a < 1. It always passes through (0, 1) and never touches the x-axis.
exam: **Definition:** f(x) = aˣ, a > 0, a ≠ 1; domain ℝ, range (0, ∞).
- a > 1: strictly increasing (growth); 0 < a < 1: strictly decreasing (decay).
- Always through (0, 1); horizontal asymptote y = 0.
- **Rules:** aˣ⁺ʸ = aˣaʸ, a⁻ˣ = 1/aˣ, (aˣ)ʸ = aˣʸ.
- Special base: **Euler's number e ≈ 2.71828**.

concepts.name: Logarithmic functions and rules
concepts.simple: log_a x asks ‘to which power must I raise a to get x?’. It undoes aˣ. It only works for x > 0.
exam: **Definition:** f(x) = logₐ x, a > 0, a ≠ 1; the **inverse of the exponential**: logₐ x = y ⇔ aʸ = x. Domain (0, ∞), range ℝ. ln x = logₑ x, log x = log₁₀ x.
**Rules:** logₐ(xy) = logₐ x + logₐ y · logₐ(x/y) = logₐ x − logₐ y · logₐ(xʳ) = r·logₐ x · **logₐ x = ln x / ln a** (change of base).
All log graphs pass through (1, 0); log₁/₂ x is decreasing.
concepts.example: ln(x + 1) + ln(x − 1) = ln 3 (need x > 1) ⇒ x² − 1 = 3 ⇒ x = ±2; domain ⇒ **only x = 2**.

concepts.name: Trigonometric functions and the unit circle
concepts.simple: Walk an angle θ around a circle of radius 1: the x-coordinate is cos θ, the y-coordinate is sin θ.
exam: For angle θ (radians), P = (cos θ, sin θ) on the unit circle; tan θ = sin θ / cos θ.
**Identities:** sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 (because x² + y² = 1 on the unit circle) · sin(θ + 2π) = sin θ · cos(θ + 2π) = cos θ · cos(x) = sin(x + π/2).
sin is odd, cos is even; both have range [−1, 1] and period 2π.
concepts.example: 2 sin θ − 1 = 0, θ ∈ [0, 2π): sin θ = 1/2, reference angle π/6, sine positive in quadrants I and II ⇒ θ = π/6 or 5π/6.

connections: **Session 3:** exp/log illustrate inverse functions; domains (log > 0) matter when solving.
**Session 5:** the derivative table covers xⁿ, eˣ, aˣ, ln x, sin x, cos x.
**Math A Lecture 1:** geometric sequences aₙ = a₁qⁿ⁻¹ are exponential in n.

questions: Solve a quadratic with the formula; interpret Δ.
Solve exponential and log equations (state the domain first).
Evaluate sin, cos, tan at standard angles; solve simple trig equations on [0, 2π).
Recognise graph shapes of the five families.
traps: After solving a log equation, **discard solutions outside the domain**.
logₐ(x + y) ≠ logₐ x + logₐ y.
Trig equations usually have **two** solutions in [0, 2π).
mistakes: Forgetting the ± in the quadratic formula.

memorize: **log(xy) = log x + log y; log(x/y) = log x − log y; log(xʳ) = r log x; logₐ x = ln x / ln a.**
**sin/cos table** for 0, π/6, π/4, π/3, π/2; **sin² + cos² = 1**; period 2π.

questions.question: Solve log₂(x) + log₂(x − 2) = 3. State the domain restriction first.
questions.model:
Domain: x > 0 and x − 2 > 0 ⇒ x > 2.
log₂(x(x − 2)) = 3 ⇒ x² − 2x = 8 ⇒ x² − 2x − 8 = 0 ⇒ x = 4 or x = −2.
Only x = 4 satisfies x > 2.
